text:
Utah played the game most teams dream of and lost it 6-1. UTA piled up 4.5 expected goals to BOS's 2.32, took 80 shot attempts to 35, and by the deserved-to-win measure came out ahead in 81 percent of simulated replays. The problem was the goalies and the special teams. Sebastian Cossa faced eight shots and allowed three goals on 0.69 expected, and Karel Vejmelka gave up three more on 1.63.

Boston scored on chances that rarely go in. Casey Mittelstadt opened the scoring in the first period on a 6 percent look, and David Pastrnak made it 2-0 on the power play on a 5 percent chance. Mason Lohrei made it 3-0 before the period ended, again on a 6 percent look. Utah had out-chanced Boston 1.66 to 0.79 in expected goals in that period and trailed by three anyway. Utah went 0 for 7 on the power play (1.22 expected goals) while BOS went 3 for 4 on 0.40 expected. Pastrnak and Morgan Geekie scored two of those in the second period, and Matthew Poitras made it 6-0 at 14:08.

At the other end, Jeremy Swayman faced 37 shots and stopped 36, saving 3.5 goals more than his workload deserved. That included a 32 percent first-period look from Jack McBain. McBain finally beat him at 9:48 of the third, a 45 percent chance, but it was the only one that got through. Pastrnak finished with two goals and two assists, and Swayman's night was just as decisive.
